notes: `הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ` -> *Beware*: the split is retained, with the ethical dative unrepresented under rule 40 and its suffix under rule 22. The competing reading fuses all three under rule 30, supported by rule 40's closing paragraph about a governed noun left with no English of its own; the split is preferable here because `הִשָּׁמֶר` alone fully licenses *Beware* — unlike `רַע בְּעֵינֶיךָ` -> *displease*, the fused word contains no sense that only the extra morphemes supply.
`לְבִלְתִּי שְׁמֹר` is divided as rule 52's gerund case directs: *in* to the preposition, *not* to `בִלְתִּי`, *keeping* to the infinitive.
The article of ha-yyom takes the demonstrative *this* under rule 41.
